claims.quote: On B200, DSpark verifies the full 5-token block (`enable_adaptive_verification:false`)
claims.claim: Author claim: the qualified B200 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash lanes use fixed DSpark k5.
claims.conditions: B200 recipe presets described in an open documentation PR.
claims.reported_result: The author reports a qualifying sweep, but no B200 comparison of fixed and adaptive verification.
claims.transfer_inference: Use fixed k5 as the reference configuration for any B200 frontier test.
claims.limitations: The PR changes guide text; an adaptive-verification effect size on B200 is unknown.

claims.quote: adaptive verification **on**, `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` | IMA within 1 min at c96 (4/4)
claims.claim: Observed report: adaptive verification with mixed prefill and decode in FULL graphs triggered illegal memory access.
claims.conditions: 2× B300, TP2, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, FlashInfer sparse attention, high-concurrency chat load.
claims.reported_result: The reporter reproduced the failure four times in four attempts.
claims.transfer_inference: A B200 adaptive-verification trial needs a graph-safety gate for mixed batches before performance calibration.
claims.limitations: This is a B300 report. Whether the same failure occurs on B200 is unknown.

claims.quote: adaptive verification **on**, `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` | stable: 15 min at c128
claims.claim: Observed report: restricting FULL graphs to decode avoided the reported failure during a shorter run.
claims.conditions: Same B300 issue and load family; adaptive verification remained enabled.
claims.reported_result: The reported arm ran for 15 minutes at c128 without the stated failure.
claims.transfer_inference: Decode-only FULL capture is a candidate safety condition for a B200 adaptive-verification experiment.
claims.limitations: A 15-minute stable run does not establish long-run safety, B200 safety, or throughput benefit.

claims.quote: Downgrade them to `UNIFORM_BATCH` and report the speculation width as the varlen decode bound
claims.claim: Author claim: limiting DSV4.1 sparse builders to uniform FULL-graph batches could keep prefill and mixed batches out of unsafe capture.
claims.conditions: Open PR covering five DSV4.1-specific metadata builders.
claims.reported_result: The author reports 82 CPU tests passed; the B300 end-to-end reproducer was not run.
claims.transfer_inference: This is a concrete graph-eligibility change to validate before enabling adaptive verification on the B200 lane.
claims.limitations: Runtime safety on B200 and any performance effect are unknown.

claims.quote: Anything the profiler measures above 1024 tokens cannot be decode.
claims.claim: Observed bug analysis: adaptive-verification cost profiling can construct a uniform decode shape that the scheduler cannot produce.
claims.conditions: Reported on 2× B200 with max_num_seqs=128 and seven speculative tokens.
claims.reported_result: The issue identifies an invalid profiling shape; it does not report a B200 performance comparison.
claims.transfer_inference: Calibrate verification cost using scheduler-reachable shapes, including mixed prefill and decode tails above the decode ceiling. Recompute that ceiling for k5 and the chosen sequence limit.
claims.limitations: The example uses k7, and its B200 cost or effect size is unknown.

claims.quote: This change profiles tail samples as schedulable mixed decode/prefill batches.
claims.claim: Author claim: the proposed profiling change supplies realistic mixed-batch shapes for adaptive-verification cost calibration.
claims.conditions: Open PR; regression tests ran on an RTX 5090.
claims.reported_result: The author reports 54 tests passed and says a full DSpark serving evaluation was not run.
claims.transfer_inference: A B200 calibration should preserve captured graph shapes and use explicit, schedulable request splits for tail samples.
claims.limitations: The tests establish the reported shape behavior, not B200 serving benefit; effect size is unknown.

claims.quote: runtime conditions and domain shift may still affect their accuracy
claims.claim: Author limitation: estimates of verification cost and acceptance benefit may become inaccurate when serving conditions change.
claims.conditions: EVICT paper excerpt concerning adaptive verification for MoE speculative decoding.
claims.reported_result: The supplied passage states a limitation; its implementation details, hardware, workload, and relevant effect size are unknown from the excerpt.
claims.transfer_inference: If using a cost-based selection policy, calibrate and check it across B200 concurrency, prefill mix, and acceptance regimes.
claims.limitations: The supplied full text has excerpt gaps. This passage is not evidence that the method is implemented in the B200 DSpark lane.

claims.quote: It was validated end to end with `nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4` and `RedHatAI/GLM-5.2-speculator.dspark` on 4× NVIDIA B300.
claims.claim: Author report: adaptive DSpark ran end to end with a sparse-MLA backend on B300.
claims.conditions: GLM-5.2, separate speculator, k7, four B300 GPUs.
claims.reported_result: The PR reports successful serving and evaluation requests; no result is asserted here for B200.
claims.transfer_inference: This supports technical plausibility only. Verify the DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash backend, graph handling, and acceptance behavior separately on B200.
claims.limitations: Model, drafter, hardware, and k differ from the fixed B200 DeepSeek k5 lane; B200 effect size is unknown.

claims.quote: With DP, ranks can choose different K values, and the EAGLE/draft proposer has K-dependent DP collectives.
claims.claim: Author claim: rank-local dynamic speculative depth can cause inconsistent collective participation under data parallelism.
claims.reported_result: The change falls back to static k under DP; no B200 verification benefit is reported.
claims.transfer_inference: Do not equate adaptive verification with changing draft k. Any B200 policy that changes k across DP ranks needs coordinated choices or a static-k fallback.
claims.limitations: The cited failure mode concerns dynamic draft depth, not proof that adaptive verification itself has this problem.

claims.quote: On A100 with TP1, two target models, four datasets, and concurrency 8–32
claims.claim: Author report: DScale evaluates a different adaptive verification design in an A100 setting.
claims.conditions: Block-diffusion speculative decoding, A100 TP1, concurrency 8–32.
claims.reported_result: The excerpt describes the evaluation setting; no B200 result is supplied.
claims.transfer_inference: Its mechanism may motivate candidate policies, but it cannot establish a gain for B200 DSpark k5.
claims.limitations: Different algorithm, hardware, models, and concurrency range; B200 effect size is unknown.

unanswered: Does adaptive verification pass sustained mixed-prefill and decode safety tests on the exact B200 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash backend and graph mode?
Are schedulable mixed-batch calibration shapes and the relevant graph-safety changes present in the B200 serving build?
What are verification cost and acceptance behavior across the actual B200 workload, concurrency, and prefill mix?
Does a safely enabled adaptive-verification policy improve any B200 throughput or latency frontier point against fixed DSpark k5? The supplied sources do not measure this.
